commits.messageBody:
Five tests covering exactly what the refactoring in #101 will touch, so that
"without changing API responses" is a claim with evidence behind it rather
than an assertion. They are green on the current code and must stay green
after the change.

- requestId keeps the format req_ plus 16 hex characters, and is taken from
  MDC when a filter put it there — this is what pins the magic number 16
- parameterName resolves a named @RequestParam, falls through when the
  @RequestParam name is blank, and resolves a @PathVariable name — the three
  paths through the two if statements that are getting braces

Scoped deliberately to the change: the class sits at 28.3% line coverage and
a full characterization suite for it exists in closed PR #96, but the column
this fills in the Lab 8 report is "which test proves this refactoring", not
"is the whole handler covered".
commits.messageHeadline: test: pin GlobalExceptionHandler behaviour touched by #101

commits.messageBody:
…rName

Closes the three Checkstyle findings named in #101, without touching what the
API returns.

- Replace Magic Number with Constant: the 16 in the requestId generator
  becomes REQUEST_ID_HEX_LENGTH, so the number has a name and a Javadoc line
  saying what it measures. It was the one findings here with teeth: nothing
  pinned the requestId format, so anyone could have changed the length and
  no test would have noticed.
- Braces on the two one-line ifs in parameterName. The second condition,
  !rp.name().isBlank(), is easy to drop by accident while reformatting, and
  dropping it silently changes which name reaches the error details.
- Wrap the 129-character line in handleMethod.

Left alone on purpose: ConstantName on the logger field (log vs LOG) is still
an open team decision from Lab 5, and EmptyLineSeparator belongs to the
project-wide rule question rather than to this class.

Behaviour unchanged, with evidence: the five tests from the previous commit
were written and run against the old code and pass here untouched. Checkstyle
findings in the class drop from 6 to 2; class line coverage rises from 28.3%
to 55.2%. Setting REQUEST_ID_HEX_LENGTH to 8 fails
generatedRequestIdKeepsItsFormat, which confirms the constant drives the
behaviour instead of merely documenting it.
